A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Muon convergence study. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E support comparison, including matching material relocated in v3.

before.justification: V2 reports original quadratic optimization, MNIST regression and MLP experiments, Shakespeare GPT-style training, and data-matrix spectral analyses.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and analyses in Figures 1–5 and Appendix D.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 retain the same gradient computation, momentum, SVD orthogonalization, and parameter updates. The revisions concern convergence analysis rather than optimizer components.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same quadratic problems, MNIST and Gaussian matrix-regression scenarios, MNIST MLP training, Shakespeare GPT-style training, and CIFAR-10/text spectral analyses.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: GD in Figure 1, GD and Adam in Figure 2, GD in the MLP experiment, and AdamW in the GPT-style experiment. Expanded related-work discussion introduces no evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Sample counts, training budgets, model dimensions, and evaluation procedures are retained, including the 120-sample MLP experiment and Table 2 settings. The quadratic objective’s added 1/2 factor in the main text already appeared in v2 Appendix E, so it reconciles documentation rather than establishing a changed experiment.

E4.justification: The rank and Gaussian-data contrasts in Figure 2, Hessian/gradient diagnostics in Figures 3–4, and supplementary spectral analyses in Appendix D are retained. No new ablation, robustness test, or empirical case study appears.

E5.justification: Both versions document the same 10,000 random quadratic samples. Neither adds optimizer-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: The Section 4.3 footnote newly states that empirical J_t does not approach zero; v2 reported only that it was usually positive. This is a limited qualitative addition. All 29 plot panels and numerical ratios, including Figure 2’s 1.57, 3.52, 0.0122, and 0.0232, are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 4.3 and Appendices B.3, B.4, and C.5 replace positivity-based case distinctions with epsilon-dependent curvature thresholds, extend small-curvature regimes, and add a stochastic O(σ³r^(3/2)epsilon^-3) claim. V3 also corrects momentum transient terms, norm inequalities, Hessian normalization, and several appendix proof steps. V2 Theorem B.1 becomes v3 Theorem 4.15; its relocation alone is not a new theorem.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: convergence analysis under several smoothness regimes, conditions for Muon’s advantage over GD, exploitation of low-rank Hessian structure, and empirical corroboration.

C2.justification: V3 qualifies the applicability of its curvature-dependent rates and uses the nonvanishing-curvature observation to motivate the main-text regimes. After Equation (6), it removes an unqualified J ≤ L assertion while retaining the single-sample conclusion. The main empirical mechanism interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix E retains the hardware, model and training specifications, Muon weight-decay and update-scaling information, and nanoGPT/Shakespeare access references. No implementation or reproducibility resource is added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 2 expands its treatment of Pethick et al. and Kovalev and newly claims a log(1/epsilon) improvement over Kovalev’s constant-step result using the paper’s existing adaptive-step analysis. The cited works themselves are unchanged.

P1.justification: V3 corrects Assumption/Lemma cross-references, expands several related-work passages, and moves the stochastic theorem and comparison discussion into the main text. It also updates author information and adds acknowledgments. Most prose and the overall section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: The document is comprehensively reformatted into the TMLR template, changing the title/author block, typography, running headers, and page composition. Figures 1–2 and Figures 3–4 move from shared pages to separate pages, and the tables are redistributed. The underlying plot panels and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: Corrected norm and Hessian formulas, momentum factors, and appendix proof steps improve mathematical consistency, while clearer rate conditions and organization aid interpretation. The gain is limited: the new small-curvature stochastic passage in Appendix B.4 switches from J* to J and omits the expectation, leaving that extension ambiguous.
